newsitem.title: UK: Tanker operator surprised at ITF blacklisting.
newsitem.headline: Tanker operator surprised at ITF blacklisting.

text.p: London Greek ship operator Polembros Shipping Ltd expressed surprise on Friday that the International Transport Workers Federation (ITF) had placed the company on its blacklist of shipowners.
The ITF said on Thursday that Polembros Maritime and Polembros Shipping Co Ltd.(Greece) had been added to its blacklist.
ITF assistant general secretary Mark Dickinson said the tanker operator had refused to negotiate any further on the introduction of ITF wage and conditions contracts for its crews.
Polembros Shipping insurance manager David Gare said he was surprised at the move and said the company had been in discussions with the ITF for one or two months.
"I am slightly disappointed because our negotiations were over one or two minor issues and things were progressing," he said.
However, Gare agreed that the company had refused to agree ITF contracts.
"We have our own contracts with our crews. They are happy with them and so are we. We do not feel it is appropriate that the ITF should be involved."
The ITF said that blacklisting would mean that all ships owned by Polembros would be targeted for action. It could involve ships being held up in port.
The ITF represents around five million transport workers around the world including seafarers, dockers, aircrew and road and rail operatives.
It is introducing a new version of its standard agreement on January 1, 1998 which will call for monthly wages for able seamen to be increased to $1200 a month from a current $1100.

The ITF added two other companies to its blacklist this week - a Philippines marine management firm and an Indonesian fishing fleet operator. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
